parentQA.a: Jack, then Ryan. Both have Carlos's number. No account manager, no call center. We stay mid-size so he's never in a bigger client's shadow.
The NFLPA caps agent fees at 3% of the playing contract, and ours go in writing before anything is signed. Nothing is paid up front, and fees are only owed on money he actually receives.

parentQA.q: How do you protect what he earns?
parentQA.a: Ryan negotiates the guarantees and injury language. We screen every advisor before he meets them, coordinate taxes, set up disability insurance and build a year-one budget. A good first contract is only the start.

parentQA.q: What happens if he gets hurt?
parentQA.a: Injury settlements, grievances and second opinions are ours to handle. Disability coverage is in place before the first snap.

parentQA.q: What if he's not drafted where we hope?
parentQA.a: It happens, and it isn't the end. Kristian Welch signed with us as an undrafted free agent in 2020 and has played six NFL seasons. The slot decides the first contract; preparation decides the second.

In business since 1986, with six clients who became the highest paid at their position. Jack Tabb played in the NFL, and Ryan Hays is a licensed attorney. We're happy to connect you with current client families.

handle: Rookie deal, extensions, guarantees, fine appeals, grievances. Ryan negotiates the language and guarantees.
Budget in year one. Every advisor and money manager screened before you meet them.
Multi-state filings coordinated. You sign; you don't chase.
Disability policy in place before the first snap. Second medical opinions on us to arrange.
Relocation, housing, car, travel. You land in a city with a place to live.
Interview prep, press, social. Nothing you say gets you in trouble.
Off-season plans, trainer access, recovery. Every year, not just the draft.
Post-career benefits filed, planning done. The career ends; the security doesn't.

cta.label: Set up a meeting
cta.sms: Hey Jack, it's Carlos. I'd like to set up a time to meet.

ask.h: Let's sit down and walk it through
ask.lede: This page is the outline. In person we'll walk you from senior season to draft night and into your second contract: where you train, what your slot could be worth, who handles what. Bring your family and your questions.

comp.h: A receiver who returns, drafted with us this spring
comp.lede: Kaden Wetjen came into the 2026 draft as a receiver and returner and went in Round 4 to the Steelers. You bring the same second way onto a roster, plus receiving tape that led the country in yards after catch through five games.
rows: 4 return TDs in 2025, most in the country
Biletnikoff watch list · preseason All-American returner
comp.foot: Jack coached Jalen Nailor at Michigan State, and Carlos reminds him of Nailor with more after the catch. Wetjen's path is the floor we'd plan from; your receiving tape is what raises it.

training.h: Pick the room that fits you
training.lede: Speed, routes, group size, distance from home. We'll walk you through each one, set up the visits, and build the plan around wherever you land.

options.name: XPE Sports
options.line: The speed lab. The three fastest 40s at the 2022 Combine came out of here, and CeeDee Lamb and Courtland Sutton have trained here in the offseason.

options.name: Bommarito Performance
options.line: One of the biggest Combine operations in the country. Stefon Diggs and DeVante Parker prepped here before their drafts.

options.name: AthElite Performance
options.line: Jeremy Holt's facility. The same staff behind the ElevaTE program that prepped Kittle, LaPorta and Kraft.

options.name: Spellman Performance
options.line: Les Spellman coaches speed and acceleration, with 20+ athletes drafted into the NFL. The closest of these to home in Alhambra, and near JB's San Diego office.

options.name: EXOS
options.line: The Athletes' Performance Institute at Fieldhouse USA. Three of the top four picks in 2022 prepped here, and so did receivers Garrett Wilson and Treylon Burks.

yours.p: If there's a trainer you already trust, we build around him.

locked.p: Where you train, who runs each piece, and the numbers we'd be chasing for you: the 40, the 10-yard split, the shuttle.

Built for the market
you come from

From Alhambra, on the Hispanic Player of the Year watch list, producing in the ACC: that's a story with a built-in audience in Southern California and well beyond it. We start building it now, not after the draft. Local partners at home first, national names as your profile grows. JB works out of San Diego, so home is a drive for us, not a flight.
